candidates.name: Primary Systemic Amyloidosis
support_spans: waxy yellow papules and plaques with purpura in the periocular, neck, axillary, trunk, and inguinal regions
anemia, abnormal liver function test results, and renal impairment with moderate proteinuria
candidates.why: The patient's combination of skin lesions, purpura, and organ dysfunction is consistent with primary systemic amyloidosis.

candidates.name: AL Amyloidosis
support_spans: anemia, abnormal liver function test results, and renal impairment with moderate proteinuria
serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP) and immunofixation urine protein electrophoresis test results were normal
candidates.why: The patient's normal SPEP and immunofixation results make AL amyloidosis less likely, but the presence of amyloidosis and organ dysfunction still suggest this possibility.
